segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When religious men complained that Jesus spent his time with sinners, he didn't argue with them. He answered with a story, about a father and his two sons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The younger son asked for his inheritance early — as if to say he wished his father were already dead. Then he left, and poured it all out on a life that emptied him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the money was gone, a famine came. He ended up feeding pigs, so hungry he would have eaten what they ate. And there, in the mud, he came to his senses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he started walking home, rehearsing a speech the whole way.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was still a long way off... when his father saw him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Old men in that world did not run. It was beneath their dignity. He ran anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He didn't wait for the speech. He wrapped his arms around his son before a single word was said.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That night the father dressed him in the finest robe, put a ring on his hand, and called for a feast — and he told everyone why.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus wasn't finished. The older son was still out in the field, like always. When he came near the house and heard the music, a servant told him: your brother is home. And he was so angry, he refused to go in.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the father left his own feast, and went out again — this time to the son who had never left.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The older son's hurt poured out. All these years I have served you. I never disobeyed you. And you never gave me even a young goat, to celebrate with my friends.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The father didn't argue with him, either. Jesus gave him the last words of the story.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Which one feels closest to where you are right now — the son who left, the father who ran to meet him, or the brother who stayed, and felt unseen?
